# ISSUE-102 plan

Make the approved target branch and commit the common baseline for issue execution and PR operations. Implement only this branch outcome; serialize implementation after the overlapping workflow/fork work and re-read its merged changes before editing. Planning makes no source changes.

## Dimensions

Risk is approved as sensitive. Advisory size: large; uncertainty: medium. This is one tightly coupled authority change, estimated to fit the 16-hour total claim budget. Seek independent security review of approval binding and fork verification; this recommendation does not change the approved gate (`none`).

## What we know

- `internal/lease/manager.go:642` (`ApproveTask`) resolves `trustedBase`, loads config/workflow there, and writes BaseSHA and task/policy digests. `trustedBase` at line 752 currently calls default-branch resolution.
- `internal/workspace/worktree.go:255` (`ResolveBaseFrom`) discovers the advertised upstream default; only absent origin falls back to local HEAD. `ResolveTrustedDefault` at line 279 has no fallback. Provisioning already takes an exact SHA (line 326 onward).
- `internal/contract/types.go:30` and `:125` define WorkUnit and SwarmConfig. `internal/contract/security.go:12` digests JSON of the WorkUnit, so an optional omitted field preserves old task digests.
- `internal/harness/scaffold.go:575` loads approved config by commit; `decodeConfig` at line 584 is the config validation mechanism. No standalone config JSON schema was found; WorkUnit JSON schemas exist in internal/contract and .swarm/contracts.
- `internal/cli/submit.go:99` independently chooses default base or accepts --base; `defaultBaseBranch` at line 284 includes a remote-less local fallback.
- `internal/pr/service.go:275` verifies PR linkage without a target-branch comparison; Status at line 334 and Rebase at line 820 share this path. Rebase compares PR BaseSHA to approved BaseSHA and supports routine reapproval.
- `internal/lease/reapprove_rebase.go:14` rechecks GitHub identity and policy before moving approval, including a final read at line 112.
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:467` compares record-submission against default branch only when resolution succeeds. `verifyForkPR` at line 622 is used by PR operations. Operations and admission synchronization tests live in internal/fork/operations_test.go; released-wire compatibility tests live in compat_released_test.go.
- `Makefile` defines make check as formatting/vet/staticcheck plus race tests. changes/unreleased/281.md demonstrates the bullet-fragment convention.

## What we're assuming

- Optional field name `base_branch` is suitable for config, WorkUnit, and state (Go BaseBranch); confirm against the merged overlapping work before implementation.
- Remote-less local repositories retain their existing current-HEAD default semantics. Named targets resolve exact local refs/heads names there; remote-backed local tests use bare upstream fixtures to exercise actual default-branch authority.
- The supplied snapshot represents the approved source. Git metadata is unavailable here (`git rev-parse HEAD` reports not a repository), so the implementer must verify paths and line references at its approved base before editing. changes/unreleased/102.md is absent in this snapshot; verify absence at approved base before creating it, otherwise modify the existing fragment.

## Open questions

- The overlapping workflow/fork changes may move symbols or add wire expectations. Step 1 reconciles these without widening scope.
- Legacy states contain no target name. Preserve decoding and default behavior as described below; changing an old task to a configured target requires explicit reapproval, never inference from candidate config.
- Live GitHub execution cannot be verified in this sandbox. Local Git fixtures and fake GitHub tracker/transport tests cover behavior; an optional maintainer smoke test is recorded in TEST_PLAN.md and does not block implementation.

## Design and implementation sequence

1. Reconcile the merged source and existing compatibility fixtures. Trace all approval, claim, submit, rebase, and fork paths, including issue edit/create rendering. Preserve operation names and all admission lists; this feature requires no new transport operation.
2. Add optional `base_branch,omitempty` to WorkUnit and SwarmConfig in internal/contract/types.go. Validate nonempty values as literal short branch names, rejecting tags, refs prefixes, revision expressions, leading option syntax, and whitespace rather than normalizing them. Extend internal/contract/parser.go (structured and Markdown parsing/FormatIssueMarkdown), edit.go if field projection requires it, internal/contract/workunit.schema.json and .swarm/contracts/workunit.schema.json. Extend internal/harness/scaffold.go decodeConfig validation and internal/harness/templates/swarm/config.yaml with an optional commented example. Update existing GitHub WorkUnit form templates under internal/harness/templates/github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ only as needed to round-trip the optional override; do not add it to community intake. Existing unset examples remain valid.
3. Add exact branch resolution alongside internal/workspace/worktree.go ResolveBaseFrom. Discover upstream default name and immutable tip first; read repository target selection only from config at that default tip. Precedence: WorkUnit override, default-branch repository base_branch, discovered default name. Fetch the selected exact refs/heads/<name> from the selected upstream using hardened Git helpers and resolve its fetched commit without trusting stale tracking refs. A missing/deleted target, failed fetch, or malformed branch fails with its name; never fall back to default, fork origin, candidate config, a tag, or cached ref. Remote-less origin fallback uses exact local heads; detached HEAD with no determinable default name requires actionable failure/reapproval before publication. Leave ledger namespace discovery and coordination admission policy on trusted upstream default.
4. In lease.Manager.ApproveTask record BaseBranch with BaseSHA in the same CAS update. Only after selecting the target load execution config, workflow, gates, role prompts, protected paths, and checks at target BaseSHA. Target config's own base_branch cannot redirect selection. Bind nonempty BaseBranch into approval policy identity using an explicit domain-separated helper; retain byte-identical old digest behavior when the optional state field is absent. Update TaskApprovalCurrent, VerifyApproval and relevant approval/carry/review binding consumers so a target-name change invalidates prior authorization even when two branches share one SHA. A matching WorkUnit override is required when present. Clear incompatible plan/revision evidence on branch change; do not carry routine policy approval across a branch change. Preserve CAS, ownership, expiry, claim fencing, and wrapped errors.
5. Legacy missing-field states continue to decode and validate with old digests and default semantics. Resolve their effective name from trusted default discovery, ignoring new repository settings until reapproval; never treat a linked PR's Base or a request parameter as the missing authority. If a legacy WorkUnit has a nonempty override, require reapproval. Persist a name only through authenticated approval, not read-only status. Branch movement does not silently move approved SHA or invalidate an otherwise pinned claim: claims/work/validation continue at recorded SHA. Reapproval fetches current target tip; routine reapproval is permitted only on the same recorded branch with existing ancestry/policy checks. Missing target blocks operations needing its live tip/publication; existing pinned work and validation can continue if the commit is available.
6. Audit internal/cli/{claim.go,work.go,validate.go,root.go}, internal/workflow/engine.go, internal/workspace/worktree.go and guidance.go, internal/validation, and lease approval checks. Keep candidate config out of authority and retain SHA-pinned provisioning/policy. Do not globally repurpose default resolution: default config remains authoritative for target selection and ledger namespace. Only adjust call sites actually selecting an execution baseline.
7. In internal/cli/submit.go derive PR target from approved state/effective legacy default. An explicitly supplied --base must exactly equal it (including explicit empty value handling); reject before push, PR creation, fork request, or completion projection, including retry paths. Check target existence freshly before publication without changing approved SHA on tip movement. Keep expected-head fencing. Update --base help to describe the assertion. The same result is required in local, GitHub, and fork modes.
8. In internal/pr/service.go verifyLink, Status and Rebase check GitHub PR.Base against recorded target before worktree, lease, rebase, or publication mutations. Report expected and observed branches with actionable recovery; never silently retarget. Fetch the recorded target tip for freshness and compare to GitHub's BaseSHA; branch movement uses the existing reapproval flow, deletion fails clearly rather than using stale refs. Include branch checks in both reads of lease.ReapproveRebase and shared mutation checks so a mid-operation retarget cannot carry approval. Preserve read-only status and existing closed/merged inspection behavior where applicable while clearly reporting mismatched target; open retargeted PR status fails. Apply the shared guard to other PR operations reached through verifyLink without adding new features.
9. In internal/fork/coordinator.go record-submission and verifyForkPR derive expected branch from coordinator state, verify upstream repository, current GitHub target, head identity, and existing claim/task/policy fences. Fail closed on resolution errors. Verify every PR revision admission path and completion re-read, not just the worker's first check. Workers cannot submit branch authority; use existing operations and optional state response field only. Audit internal/fork/transport.go and internal/lease/fork_request.go for strict request decoding and round-trip state preservation. Preserve released fixtures, protocol version, absent-field JSON behavior, Operations, transport dispatch and both checked-in/generated workflow admission lists.
10. Extend the tests in TEST_PLAN.md, then docs/developer.md and SECURITY.md with target precedence, default-branch selection trust, target-SHA execution policy, reapproval, legacy behavior, --base assertion and retarget recovery. Add changes/unreleased/102.md only after approved-base absence verification; never edit CHANGELOG directly. Run required checks and independent review focused on branch-authority attacks.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to recheck against source, not authority over approved inputs or gates.

- Entry points: contract WorkUnit/SwarmConfig (`internal/contract/types.go:30,125`), DigestWorkUnit (`security.go:12`), config loader (`internal/harness/scaffold.go:575`), ResolveBaseFrom/ResolveTrustedDefault (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:255,279`), ApproveTask/trustedBase/TaskApprovalCurrent/VerifyApproval (`internal/lease/manager.go:642,752,2103,2107`), ReapproveRebase (`internal/lease/reapprove_rebase.go:14`), submit base selection (`internal/cli/submit.go:99,284`), verifyLink/Status/Rebase (`internal/pr/service.go:275,334,820`), coordinator submission/verifyForkPR (`internal/fork/coordinator.go:467,622`).
- Extend existing tests: internal/contract/{parser_test.go,edit_test.go,parser_security_test.go}; internal/harness/ledger_namespace_test.go and scaffold tests; internal/lease/{manager_test.go,approval_error_test.go}; internal/workspace/{upstream_remote_test.go,policy_test.go,bundle_guidance_test.go}; internal/cli/{cli_test.go,upstream_remote_test.go,untouched_base_test.go,pr_test.go,submit_freshness_test.go}; internal/pr/{service_test.go,work_preflight_test.go}; internal/fork/{fork_test.go,transport_security_test.go,transport_test.go,operations_test.go,compat_released_test.go}. Add cases to existing files where practical.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/contract ./internal/harness ./internal/lease ./internal/workspace ./internal/validation ./internal/workflow ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork`; `go test -race ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork`; final `go build ./...` and `make check` plus the compiled required checks listed in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: config decoding is strict YAML rather than a separate config schema; optional WorkUnit fields use omitempty and task digest marshals the struct; default resolution currently has remote-less HEAD fallback. Evidence above comes from source reads. Approved-base file existence remains to be checked with Git metadata.
- Reopen the plan if merged work changes approval/wire semantics incompatibly, the branch setting requires a new transport operation, or the cycle no longer fits 16 hours. Tags, backports, multiple targets, and broader rebase redesign need separate WorkUnits.
- What this change breaks: submit.go --base help/default behavior and CLI tests expecting arbitrary overrides must assert matching recorded targets instead; fork coordinator default-base expectations must use approved targets and fail on discovery failure. PR service/rebase tests and fake PullRequest fixtures must supply consistent Base names. Preserve untouched-base, policy-pinning, lease fencing, legacy omitted JSON/digest and released-coordinator tests unchanged in strength. Parser/render/edit round-trip tests and generated WorkUnit form/config assertions need optional-field coverage. Keep migration/ledger namespace tests default-branch-only. Update docs/developer.md and SECURITY.md branch explanations; preserve README and unrelated docs/templates. Search these symbols again after overlapping work merges to catch added call sites.

Add regression tests for missing branches, branch movement/deletion and fork transport tampering as needed by security invariants; keep scope to stated branch outcome. # ISSUE-102 test plan

Use table-driven local-backend CLI tests with temporary bare Git remotes and fake GitHub trackers. Give default, release and LTS branches distinct commits and policy contents, and include two branch names sharing one commit. No live credentials or publication are needed. All security regression cases must fail against old behavior.

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete coverage | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Unset preserves default behavior | Omitted config/WorkUnit/state fields retain default selection, JSON and task/policy digests; remote default is not assumed to be main. Remote-less local origin fallback remains supported. Explicit missing named upstream fails. Existing ledger namespace authority remains on upstream default. | contract parser/digest, harness config, lease approval, workspace upstream and CLI fixture tests; focused command below |
| 2. Repository setting/override pins fetched tip and state branch; missing branch fails | Default config selects release; WorkUnit selects LTS over release; target config attempting to select another target is ignored. Dirty checkout/fork config cannot select target. Verify state branch+SHA and target policy/gate. Reject invalid names, tags, revision expressions and missing branch with named error and no approval mutation. Test stale tracking refs after deletion and fetch failures. Changing override stales task approval; changing state branch with unchanged SHA fails policy binding. Reapproval records new tip; branch changes invalidate old evidence even at same SHA. | lease manager, harness/parser and local CLI approval tests |
| 3. Worktrees/policy use approved SHA | Claim/work provision release SHA, not latest default or moved release tip. Distinct target checks/protected paths/prompts/workflow are used; candidate files cannot relax them. Move/delete target after approval: pinned work/validation continue with available SHA; operations needing live branch fail by name. Reapproval changes baseline only through existing authorized transitions. | workspace policy/bundle tests, CLI untouched-base and work/validate tests, workflow/validation suites |
| 4. Submit uses recorded branch; mismatching --base fails before publication | Local and fake GitHub submissions record exact release target; omitted and equal --base succeed; different, invalid and explicitly empty --base fail before push, tracker CreatePullRequest, gateway requests or projection. Include completed retry path. Target tip advance does not repin approval; target deletion/fetch failure refuses publication despite cached refs. Fork uses upstream target, not fork origin default. | CLI submit/upstream/freshness fixtures, fork coordinator submission tests |
| 5. PR status/rebase use recorded branch and reject retarget | Open PR release target reports correctly and rebases to fetched release tip under existing approval rules. Default tip movement is irrelevant. PR retarget to default or another branch (including identical SHA) fails status/rebase clearly with both names before mutations. Deletion and branch-fetch errors fail without stale-ref rebase. Same-branch advance requires existing explicit/routine reapproval; non-descendant movement retains existing refusal. Retarget between initial read and reapproval/completion read fails, as do resume/continue paths. | internal/pr service and local CLI pr tests, lease routine-reapproval tests |
| 6. Local unit matrix and make check | Run all above on local tracker/store with real temporary Git refs; extend fake GitHub/fork coverage and released-wire compatibility below; formatting, vet, staticcheck and race tests pass. | focused and final commands below |

Additional adversarial coverage tied to criteria 2–5:

- Fork record-submission and every PR revision operation reject actual GitHub target mismatch; upstream lookup failure cannot bypass comparison. Forged worker parameters, replayed state/comment content, stale claim IDs, tampered response branch fields and dropped optional fields cannot change coordinator authority or authorize a nondefault target. Existing transport response verification must reconcile returned authority with upstream authoritative state where it relies on response fields; local response tampering alone cannot grant publication authority.
- Keep old ForkRequest and IssueState payloads decodable, do not add required wire fields or bump protocol version, and retain all released-coordinator operation fixtures. New absent fields must not change canonical payload/digest expectations. A new worker encountering legacy state uses trusted default semantics; nondefault execution needs coordinator-recorded approval.
- Test branch target changes at same SHA, task override edit after approval, branch deletion after a previous successful fetch, and PR retarget during GitHub rereads. Assert no state writes, pushes or PR publication on rejected paths, and preserve ErrClaimFence wrapping.
- Run TestOperationListsStayInSync and the complete operations/compatibility suites; preserve Operations, transport dispatch, and both workflow admission lists. No added operation is planned.

Commands (from an implementation checkout with approved dependencies and writable caches):

```bash
go test ./internal/contract ./internal/harness ./internal/lease ./internal/workspace ./internal/validation ./internal/workflow ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork
go test -race ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork
go test ./internal/fork -run 'TestOperationListsStayInSync|TestReleasedCoordinatorAcceptsAllOperations'
go build ./...
make check
```

Also execute the compiled approved required checks directly: formatting (`gofmt -s -l .`, require empty output), `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go tool staticcheck ./...`, and `go test ./...`. Avoid redundant repeats where the same checks have just passed through make check. Validate changed Markdown links, shell snippets with `bash -n`, schema parity, generated template expectations and documented flags against Cobra definitions. Confirm only a changes/unreleased fragment changes, not CHANGELOG. Independent review should trace branch choice from trusted default config through approval, pinned execution, submit, PR reapproval, and coordinator verification.

Optional maintainer smoke test after implementation: in a disposable GitHub repository with a release branch, approve a target WorkUnit, inspect recorded SHA/name, submit a Draft PR, advance release and exercise status/rebase, then retarget the PR and confirm refusal. Repeat through a contributor fork if available. This checks live service integration; local fixtures provide required automated coverage and implementation does not wait on this environment.

Planning validation: source and existing test fixtures inspected; no implementation checks were run because this phase writes planning artifacts only. Git metadata is absent in the planning snapshot; implementer verifies new fragment absence at approved base before creation.

# ISSUE-102 plan review (sensitive profile)

The plan is mostly sound. It reads target selection only from trusted default-branch config, gives the WorkUnit override precedence, resolves the branch exactly and fails closed, loads policy at the target SHA, binds the branch name into approval identity, treats `--base` as an assertion, checks PR retargets, and verifies GitHub state on the coordinator side. Its digest and wire analysis also mostly holds up against the source. But it misses one existing code path that silently moves an approved task to the default branch tip at claim time. It also leaves the default-case state and digest format undecided, and that format decides both AC1 and compatibility with old released workers. Both need fixing before implementation.

## Audit

| Item | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC1 unset → unchanged | Gap | Plan doesn't say whether the unset case persists `BaseBranch` or changes `PolicyDigest` (R2). |
| AC2 approve pins target tip, records name, missing fails by name | Covered | Steps 3–4. TEST_PLAN row 2 covers missing, invalid, stale-ref, and same-SHA cases. |
| AC3 worktrees/policy from base_sha | **Gap** | `prepareClaimBase` re-pins fresh claims to the default tip (R1). |
| AC4 submit uses recorded branch; `--base` mismatch fails pre-publish | Covered | Step 7 covers retry/completed path, explicit-empty, and fork. |
| AC5 rebase/status use recorded branch; retarget stops | Covered | Step 8 covers both ReapproveRebase reads and the shared verifyLink guard. Local fixture mechanism needed (R4). |
| AC6 local-backend matrix + make check | Covered with R4 | `Makefile:44` `check: lint race` confirmed. |
| Constraint: repo setting only from default-branch trusted config | Covered with R3 | Step 3. Must explicitly exclude the `loadTrustedUpstreamConfig` candidate fallback. |
| Constraint: policy/protected_paths/prompts from target base_sha | Covered | Step 4. `LoadConfigAt`/`LoadWorkflowAt`/`PolicyTreeDigest` already take a SHA (`manager.go:672-686`). |
| Constraint: schemas/templates/docs/SECURITY/fragment | Covered | Both `workunit.schema.json` copies have `additionalProperties: false` (line 78), so both need the field. No config JSON schema exists; `decodeConfig` is strict YAML (`scaffold.go:583`). `changes/unreleased/102.md` is absent. |
| Protected paths | OK | `allow_harness_changes: true`. Plan touches `.swarm/contracts/**` and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/**` only as needed. |
| Evidence ("What we know") | Mostly verified | Line drift is minor: `types.go:27/128` (not 30/125), `ResolveTrustedDefault` at 277. The fork "optional state response field" claim is wrong (R5). |
| Scope | OK | Tags, backports, and multiple targets are excluded. The live smoke test is optional and doesn't block. |

## Required revisions

**R1 — Claim-time base re-pin is not addressed (blocking, security).**

- What happens now: `internal/lease/manager.go:861-866` calls `prepareClaimBase` for every fresh claim. `internal/lease/claim_base.go:42` resolves `m.trustedBase()`, which is the *default* branch tip. If that differs from `original.BaseSHA`, it rewrites `BaseSHA`/`PolicyDigest` to the default tip. The only checks are an unchanged policy tree and ancestry.
- Why that breaks this feature: a release-targeted task whose release tip is an ancestor of the default branch (common when a release branch has no commits of its own yet) with an identical policy tree gets moved to the default tip at claim. That silently chooses another target, which violates AC3 and the "never silently choose another target" requirement. This runs on the coordinator for fork `acquire` too.
- The plan doesn't name this path anywhere. Step 5 says "claims/work/validation continue at recorded SHA", which also contradicts the existing, intended re-pin of untouched tasks. That changes default behavior (AC1) if taken literally.
- Revise steps 4–6 to:
  - (a) make `prepareClaimBase` resolve the *recorded* branch's fetched tip, with the same exact-ref fail-closed resolver as approve;
  - (b) keep the existing fresh-claim re-pin semantics on the same branch only;
  - (c) for legacy or unset states, keep re-pinning to the trusted default. Never let a newly added repo setting redirect a legacy state at claim.
- Add tests: release-targeted fresh claim with default advanced and release as its ancestor stays on release; release advanced re-pins to the new release tip; release deleted fails by name; legacy state plus new repo setting still uses default.

**R2 — Decide the default-case persistence and digest format explicitly (blocking, compatibility).**

- Step 4 says "record BaseBranch with BaseSHA" and "bind nonempty BaseBranch into approval policy identity". If an unset approval records the discovered default name (e.g. `main`), every new approval changes `PolicyDigest`. Then `TaskApprovalCurrent` (`manager.go:2103`) in released binaries, which don't know about the new binding, fails for ordinary tasks. That breaks AC1 and v0.8.0 worker compatibility.
- Specify: when neither the repo setting nor the WorkUnit override is present, persist no `BaseBranch` and leave `DigestApprovedPolicy` byte-identical. The effective name then comes from trusted default discovery.
- Specify that a nondefault target *does* change `PolicyDigest`, and the WorkUnit override changes `TaskDigest` (`security.go:12` marshals the struct). As a result, released workers and coordinators that drop the field fail closed rather than running against the wrong branch.
- Add tests:
  - an unset approval's state JSON and `PolicyDigest` are golden-equal to today's;
  - a nondefault approval fails the old-formula `TaskApprovalCurrent` check;
  - a WorkUnit parsed without the override field has a different digest than one with it.
- Document in docs/developer.md, SECURITY.md, and the fragment that old binaries reject a `.swarm/config.yaml` containing `base_branch` (strict YAML, `scaffold.go:585`) and refuse tasks with nondefault targets.

**R3 — Name the candidate-config fallback that must not feed selection.**

`internal/cli/root.go:250-263` (`loadTrustedUpstreamConfig`, used for fork mode at `root.go:385`) falls back to `harness.LoadConfig(root)`, the local checkout, when upstream resolution fails. Step 3 should state that target selection never reads `base_branch` from this function or any other fallback path. Selection runs only in `ApproveTask`/`prepareClaimBase` on the coordinator. Fork workers learn the target only from coordinator-written state. Add a test where the fork-worker checkout's config sets `base_branch` and upstream resolution fails. Neither the selected target nor any submit/rebase expectation may change.

**R4 — Specify how the local-backend retarget is simulated.**

`LocalTracker` has no API to change a PR's base (`internal/tracker/local.go`). AC6 requires a local-backend retarget test. TEST_PLAN should state that the test mutates `PullRequest.Base` in local tracker state through a test-only helper, with no production retarget command. It should also note that `refreshPRRefs` (`local.go:653`) keeps a stale stored `BaseSHA` when the base branch is deleted, so the deletion case must assert on the fresh-fetch failure, not on tracker data.

**R5 — Correct the fork evidence.**

`ForkResult` (`internal/fork/transport.go:26`, `testdata/releasedv080/transport.go:19`) carries no state. Workers read `IssueState` from the state ref. Drop "optional state response field" from step 9, and make sure no `ForkResult` or `ForkRequest` field is added. Both are decoded with `DisallowUnknownFields` in released coordinators and workers.

## Non-blocking notes

- `fork/coordinator.go:467` currently skips the base check whenever `resolveDefaultBase` errors *or* returns `""` (`coordinator.go:665-676` swallows errors). Step 9's fail-closed change should replace this helper for the target comparison rather than wrap it.
- Cobra can't tell `--base ""` from an omitted flag without `Flags().Changed("base")`. Test both.
- Re-check line references after the overlapping work merges, as the plan already says.

## LESSONS

- Also audit callers of `trustedBase()`, not just `ApproveTask`. `prepareClaimBase` re-pins fresh claims to whatever `trustedBase()` returns.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Security-review trusted target selection and exact target binding end to end, including default-branch trusted config, approved task override, state/review bindings, issue claim/work/submit, local/github and fork coordinator, PR retarget and rebase/status behavior, old released-worker compatibility and fail-closed missing branch/config. No authority from candidate or fork config, no silently choosing another target or weakening policy. Identify acceptance gaps and actual schema/default path compatibility. Write only REVIEW.md and optional LESSONS.md.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->
